messages:
Alex: Quick sync 1: we flipped the coalesce jitter dist to a right-skewed variant for a small perf run and observed unexpected kernel churn + KV hotset pressure. Posting the short log and a proposed canary.

Alex: Baseline (rectangular 0-5ms): p50=9.7ms, p95=68ms, mean_batch=2.8, kv_hit=93.2%, kernel=fused_attn dominant
Alex: Skewed-exp (lambda=1.1, tail to ~12ms): p50=12.1ms, p95=140ms, mean_batch=4.9, kv_hit=81.0%, kernel=aten majority

Alex: Sample harness trace:
```
[batcher] avg_coalesce=7.3ms
microbatch_interval=2ms
coalesce_jitter=exp_right_skew(lambda=1.1,max_cap=12ms)
token_budget=28
kernel_decisions: fused_attn:58, aten:242
kv_evictions_rate +22% vs baseline
reason: fused_abort=kv_alignment_failure (max_prefix_len increased)
```

Maria: Aten selection path indicates fused kernel's precondition failed. The logs indicate the merged batch had a wider max-prefix distribution after coalescing. No model checkpoint or quantization change?

Alex: No. Same model and quantization. Coalesce caused more cross-prefix merges which increased max_seq and tripped the fused kernel's "kv_shape_check".

Sam: Hypothesis: right-skewed jitter increases probability that older short-prefix reqs wait long enough to be joined with longer ones, producing heterogeneous batches. That raises max_prefix_len and triggers fused fallback.

Priya: The KV miss spike explains the p95 blowup. We should not promote this change wide without canary rollback thresholds. Propose: abort if kv_hit drops >4% absolute OR p95 > 110ms sustained for 2 mins.

Alex: Canary proposal:
- scope: 5% of traffic
- duration: 90 minutes
- matrix: coalesce_jitter=[rectangular(0-5), clipped_exp(lambda=1.1,cap=6), exp_right_skew(lambda=1.1,cap=12)] x token_budget=[28,40] x microbatch_interval=[2ms,3ms]
- primary metrics: kv_cache_hit_rate, kernel_type_fraction, batch_size_p50/p95, request_p95
- rollback: any matrix cell that trips either trigger or increases kv_evictions by >15%

Maria: Suggest adding a "prefix-homogeneity gate": only coalesce requests if their prefix_length delta <= 6 tokens. That should prevent mixing very-short and long prefixes.

Sam: Also test token_budget=40. Earlier experiments showed larger token budgets decrease kernel switching because fused kernel gets stable aligned batches.

Alex: Local repro command to iterate faster:
```
./perf_runner --model=redwood-13b --workload=prod-replay \
  --microbatch_interval=2 --coalesce_jitter=clipped_exp:1.1:6 \
  --token_budget=40 --run_secs=600 --delta_seq_gate=6
```

ci-bot: queued perf job -> s3://redwood-perf/runs/1769998888/ (artifacts: pprof, batch_hist.csv, kernel_decisions.log)

Priya: I'll add an alert rule: page on p95 > 110ms for 2 consecutive 1m windows OR absolute kv_hit drop >4% from baseline for a 5m window. Also add dashboard tiles for per-prefix kv_hotness and eviction timestamps.

Maria: When we collect logs, please include per-batch candidate seq_len stats and the "decision_reason" string that runtime emits so we can correlate fused aborts to specific coalescing events.

Sam: If clipped_exp looks promising, we can add adaptive clipping: dynamically lower clip if kv_evictions rise above threshold.

Alex: I'll run the first cell (clipped_exp, token_budget=28, microbatch_interval=2ms) in canary tomorrow 09:00 PST and post the artifact links. Tagging @Maria @Sam @Priya for on-call review during the window. Thanks :thumbsup:
